dispositions.evidence: Round-2 minor: manifest label round-trip shape asymmetry between package._normalized_specs and record._manifest_input_spec. The rebuilt package digest still matches (the default label is the path stem either way); the missing test/canonicalization is deferred to issue #33 item 2.

Round-2 minor: the fail-closed branch in controller._put_record_checks is not covered by a test. Deferred to issue #33 item 1; the branch itself is present and the round-1 authority tests cover the refusal path.
Round-2 minor: REVIEWING's review_record_pr refuses a historical DRAFT_OPENED row with no persisted pr detail. Fail-closed by design; the explicit historical-row path is deferred to issue #33 item 3.

findings.evidence: the manifest round-trip between the build side and the rebuild side is shape-asymmetric for label-less contract/gate specs — `_normalized_specs` encodes them as a bare `rel` while `_manifest_input_spec` always re-encodes them as `rel:label` — yet no test in the diff rebuilds a record whose manifest carries a non-empty contract or gate spec: every rebuild fixture renders with empty specs (test_manifest_record_package_deleted_*, test_check_rebuilds_from_manifest_without_package_file, TestCiGateManifestRecord), and test_manifest_out_records_scope_flags_in_cli_order only inspects the stored JSON without ever rebuilding from it. If the package header renders the spec string verbatim, `check` falsely refuses rebuilt records with unlabeled inputs and the T1 fresh-clone guarantee is unproven for them; the byte-determinism invariant the fix relies on stays green under either behavior.
findings.required_change: add a rebuild test that renders with a label-less and a label-carrying contract/gate spec, deletes the package file, and asserts `check` exits 0 with a digest match, or canonicalize `_normalized_specs` and `_manifest_input_spec` to one shared spec form so the round-trip is shape-identical by construction

findings.evidence: the new fail-closed guard in _put_record_checks ('record is None' -> put("review_head_match", False, "record unreadable — head match cannot be established (fail closed)") and the matching no_open_blocker_major branch) is exercised by no test in the package: every READY_FOR_REVIEW / MERGE_ELIGIBLE fixture in the tools/tests/test_controller.py diff (test_ready_for_review_record_head_rule, test_ready_for_review_refuses_open_blocker_major, test_merge_eligible_refuses_unresolvable_head_sha, TestMergeEligibleRecordHeadRule, TestMultirepoSetLevel.merge_ev) seeds an existing fake_record, so a production change flipping that first branch to put("review_head_match", True, ...) leaves every test green while a refused transition persists a check_results row claiming a head match on an unreadable record; only the review-record-path refusals at REVIEWING (test_reviewing_refuses_missing_record_path) are covered, and they use the separate REVIEWING put() calls, not _put_record_checks
findings.required_change: add controller fixtures that drive READY_FOR_REVIEW and MERGE_ELIGIBLE with review_record pointing at a missing (or uncontained/unparseable) record directory and assert the persisted check_results carry review_head_match=False and no_open_blocker_major=False with the fail-closed details, anchored at the _put_record_checks hunk in tools/controller.py

findings.evidence: REVIEWING's new `review_record_pr` check derives the expected pr only from the persisted DRAFT_OPENED evidence detail, and the diff's own comment acknowledges rows that carry no such detail (`None when the row carries no evidence detail — historical rows are read, never re-judged`). For such a row `pr_expect` is None and the check refuses (fail closed) ever reaching REVIEWING; `no_duplicate_trigger` also refuses a compensating second DRAFT_OPENED request, so a pre-cutover story parked at DRAFT_OPENED with a detail-less row has no request path to REVIEWING at all — the backward-compat fold promise covers mechanism values but not this evidence-detail shape.
findings.required_change: when the DRAFT_OPENED row carries no pr_number detail, accept an evidence-supplied pr_number at REVIEWING and match it against the record's pr (instead of refusing), or document an explicit override path for detail-less historical rows
